r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Inherited crew rules hold. Minimal change, no speculative abstraction (four primitives, one CLI, nothing more). Behavior is test-led and adversarial, not round-trip-confirming. Fail-visibly is honored at the CLI boundary: three distinct exit codes (0 answered / 1 invalid query / 2 no such episode) so an unanswerable query never masquerades as an empty result, and an unknown field RAISES rather than returning []. C5 verified independently: no ranking/scoring/similarity import, results carry no score-like key, id-sort only, and neighbours joined on two keys do not sort above neighbours joined on one. One doc-vs-code nit inside query_episodes.py: select_episodes' docstring says the field name is 'validated once, up front, against the FIRST episode scanned' -- the code actually validates it against _FIELD_READERS before the scan (which is better). Stale prose, not a defect.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: One genuine divergence Commander must reconcile, routed to g4 rather than charged here. EPISODE_STORE.md section 8 states that 'enumerate non-retired' obtains its candidate set from iter_episode_ids(include_retired=False) then confirms each id through is_episode_in_ordinary_search(), and that select and neighbours 'both scan the same iter_episode_ids(include_retired=False) candidate set'. Section 10 lists 'enumerate non-retired' as a g3 deliverable. The shipped code instead calls iter_episode_ids(root, include_retired=True) with no membership filter anywhere, and builds no non-retired variant. Under the currently-bound Option-B placeholder adapter include_retired is a no-op, so behavior is identical TODAY -- but the frozen contract now describes primitives that do not exist as described, and I demonstrated the consequence: a retired episode is returned by all three scanning primitives while is_episode_in_ordinary_search() correctly says False, contradicting section 7's settled 'excluded from ordinary rhyme-search'. I judge the implementer's deferral CORRECT (wiring the membership seam now is retirement-dependent retrieval, which this handoff explicitly excludes and which section 10 assigns to g4), so the fix is a DOC reconciliation at g4: section 8's composition sentences and section 10's g3 bullet must move to g4 when the layout binds. Everything else reconciles: the five-seam table is honored exactly (store root, resolve_episode_path, iter_episode_ids used; is_episode_in_ordinary_search named-but-unused by design; apply_retirement untouched), and I proved the seam discipline is enforced by a live test, not just by convention. Also confirmed rather than rediscovered: the Windows core.autocrlf hazard is genuinely PINNED -- the test asserts writer bytes are LF-only, that the two worktrees' bytes differ by line endings at most, that git ls-files --eol reports i/lf, and, when CRLF is actually live in the environment, that raw bytes DIFFER while the parsed records are equal. That is a real pin, not prose, and issue #319 carries it for #308.

r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards â€” an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. Do NOT silently skip this item.

an override (smell not flagged because a standard wins) needs a logged reason
r6-fowler.finding: Pass recorded to .agent-work/301/g3-review/fowler-pass.json; verify_fowler_pass.py exits 0 (smells=12, flagged=4, overridden=3). FLAGGED (all observation-grade, none blocking): duplicated-code -- the unknown-field error message is built twice, byte-identical, in field_values() and select_episodes(); primitive-obsession -- the composite join key is a NUL-joined string inside a tuple that is already a tuple; speculative-generality -- JOIN_KEYS is DEAD, read by nothing, while neighbours()'s docstring claims completeness 'over all of JOIN_KEYS', so the completeness claim and the code implementing it (_join_key_values, which hardcodes both keys) can drift with nothing detecting it -- a real hazard when #308 extends the join set; comments-as-deodorant -- two docstrings have already drifted from the code (select_episodes' 'validated against the FIRST episode scanned', and the naive fixture's '## Mechanical block'). OVERRIDDEN with logged standards: long-method (the 80-line C3 acceptance test -- the length IS the assertion, and I verified the mid-method still-absent check is what catches a same-directory simulation); feature-envy (EPISODE_STORE.md section 7's five-seam table REQUIRES retrieval to call the writer's seams by name -- the envy is the contract, and I proved inlining goes red); message-chains (writer() re-resolves sys.modules on every call to guarantee one canonical grammar module, which the layout-flip test depends on).

r4a-omission-fixture.title: Silent-omission fixture: realistic naive, or strawman?
r4a-omission-fixture.imperative: Judge whether the naive implementations in the silent-omission fixtures are realistic naive implementations rather than strawmen built to lose.
r4a-omission-fixture.finding: REALISTIC, not strawmen. naive_select_dict_collapse folds '- key: value' lines into a dict -- the single most common way anyone writes a Markdown field reader, and it loses on the store's OWN genuinely-repeated field (artifact-ref), not on a contrivance. naive_select_substring over-returns on a real prefix collision (g1 vs g1-implement) -- the opposite error, so 'exact' is pinned from both sides. naive_neighbours_first_key_wins reads as an entirely sensible 'find shared artifacts, else fall back to same role+step'. The fixtures are also not rigged: seed_ref_position_fixture puts TARGET first, middle and last, so the collapse loses on 2 of 3 rather than on a single hand-placed record, and the property is asserted as set(naive) < set(ours), not as a magic number. One cosmetic mismatch: naive_select_dict_collapse's docstring says it reads the '## Mechanical block' but the code scans every '- key: value' line in the whole file; the demonstrated outcome is identical for artifact-ref, so this is a comment nit, not a rigged fixture.

r4b-uncovered-omission.title: Hunt a silent omission the fixture does NOT cover
r4b-uncovered-omission.imperative: Find a record that should be returned and is not (or should not be and is), in the SHIPPED retrieval, outside what the fixtures cover.
r4b-uncovered-omission.finding: HUNT PERFORMED, DEFECT FOUND, adjudicated BELOW the block threshold. Probe: scratchpad/probe_omission.py against the repo's real scripts. FINDING-1 (ranked first in REVIEW_RESULT, recommended as an authorized one-line fix-now): select_episodes(root, field, values) does set(values), so a caller passing a bare STRING silently degrades to CHARACTER membership. Demonstrated with two episodes, role=implementer and role=i: the string form select_episode_ids(root, role, implementer) returned the role=i episode -- the WRONG record -- and omitted the right one, with no exception. The natural caller idiom is the buggy one, and the future callers (#305, #308) are agent-written. Unreachable from the CLI because argparse action=append always yields a list, which is why no test caught it. FINDING-2: enumerate_episodes ends with an 'if ep is not None' filter, dropping an enumerated-but-unresolvable id with zero signal (demonstrated by stubbing resolve_episode_path to None for one id: 2 ids enumerated, 1 record returned, select returned nothing). Unreachable under either bound adapter today, but a git merge/checkout landing between the scan and the read is a live race for a store whose whole premise is content arriving via git; doctrine says fail visibly. FINDING-3: a retired episode is returned by enumerate, select and neighbours while is_episode_in_ordinary_search() says False -- deferred to g4 by the implementer and explicitly excluded by this handoff, carried to r5 as a doc/code divergence. ADJUDICATION: none of global-crew's block triggers fires -- close criteria C2-C5 are met and I proved each test can go red; evidence reproduced exactly; scope respected; no contract decision needed. Routed the way g2's artifact-ref defect was routed (authorized fix-now), not as a gate failure.

consolidation.summary: APPROVE with findings. All four close criteria met and independently demonstrated, not accepted on report. C2 is a REAL process boundary (subprocess + sys.executable, three distinct OS pids, child reports its own getpid inside the answer, session 2 receives only a store root and an id whose slug carries none of the asserted content, session 1 already exited) and C3 is a REAL git worktree boundary (real git init + two real worktree adds, .git-is-a-FILE with a gitdir: pointer, absent -> still-absent-after-local-commit -> present-only-after-merge observed). Eight mutations run in an out-of-repo mirror proved every acceptance test can go red: M1 fake pid, M2 not-found silently rc 0, M3 statement truncated in transit, M4 first-key-wins neighbours, M5 collapsed artifact-ref, M6 non-surgical amend, M7/M7b same-directory worktree simulation (still red with the anti-aliasing guard neutered), M8 inlined glob + status check. Naive fixtures are realistic, not strawmen. Findings, none blocking: (1) MEDIUM demonstrated defect -- select_episodes does set(values), so a bare-string values argument degrades to CHARACTER membership and returns the WRONG episode silently; one-line guard, recommended as an authorized fix-now on the g2-artifact-ref precedent; (2) MEDIUM doc reconciliation -- EPISODE_STORE.md sections 8 and 10 describe include_retired=False composition and a g3 'enumerate non-retired' that were correctly deferred to g4, so the frozen contract now misdescribes what shipped; (3) LOW enumerate_episodes silently drops an unresolvable id; (4-7) LOW Fowler flags -- dead JOIN_KEYS constant with a drift hazard, duplicated error message, two already-drifted docstrings, NUL-joined composite key. Repo left untouched: git status shows only the implementer's 2 modified + 1 new, episodes/ holds only README.md.
